page: Microsoft Azure F4alds_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features 4 physical cores mapped to 4 dedicated vCPUs with a peak clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The CPU cache layout includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, backed by vector extensions such as AVX-512, VNNI, and BF16. System memory is sized at 8.0 GB, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It bundles a 472 GB local NVMe SSD for high-speed scratch storage but includes no discrete GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results highlight exceptional single-thread capabilities. In stress-ng single-core tests and Geekbench single-core evaluations, the instance ranks in the top tier, bolstered by single-threaded text processing, bzip3 decompression, and gzip compression throughput. It similarly achieves top-tier generation speeds when running small 135M language models. Multi-core benchmarks, including multi-threaded Geekbench, stress-ng, Clang compilation, and ray tracing, place in the middle tier, aligning with its 4-thread execution footprint. Memory bandwidth registers at 53.52 GB/sec read and 34.56 GB/sec write for uncached transfers, while static web serving achieves 10.41 GB/sec and Redis registers 13.15 million SET operations per second.

The primary tradeoff of the F4alds_v7 lies in its low memory footprint relative to its CPU compute potential. While its 4.5 GHz clock provides competitive compute per core, memory-intensive jobs and medium-sized LLM prompt processing exhibit notable performance constraints. The local NVMe disk mitigates I/O bottlenecks for disk-bound temporary operations, offering high efficiency for CPU-dense batch jobs, compilation pipelines, web application hosting, and specialized microservices without incurring the expense of larger memory allocations.
description: Microsoft Azure F4alds_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine configured with 4 dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 vCPUs running at up to 4.5 GHz, accompanied by 8.0 GB of memory and a bundled 472 GB local NVMe SSD. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance provides a 1:2 memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU without hardware GPU acceleration. In benchmark assessments, the EPYC architecture delivers top-tier single-core performance across stress-ng and Geekbench tests, alongside high throughput in compression and small-model inference. Multi-core performance, memory bandwidth, and Redis throughput register within average ranges, reflecting the 4-core boundary. Because memory capacity is tightly bounded, resource saturation can occur during large-scale data tasks or medium-model prompt processing. The F4alds_v7 offers strong cost efficiency for high-frequency compute, fast local scratch caching, CI/CD runners, batch processing, and latency-sensitive web services where single-thread instruction throughput takes precedence over deep memory allocations.
